title: My First Animal Sounds (Part 1)
developmental_focus: Vocabulary explosion + auditory-verbal imitation. Ages 2-3 benefit from animal-sound books more than plain vocabulary lists because they combine label learning (animal name) with a sound the child can imitate, plus a natural call-and-response reading rhythm ('The cow says...? Moo!') that keeps the child actively participating during read-aloud.
safety_notes: One animal, one clear scene, one sound word per page -- no split-panel or multi-element compositions (lesson learned from the ABC book: complex single-shot compositions are not reliable with free image generators).
Lion depicted as a smiling, non-threatening cub, never a roaring/aggressive adult pose.
Bee depicted as a friendly, rounded, non-threatening cartoon with no emphasized stinger.
No animal shown in a predatory, aggressive, or frightening pose; all animals smiling/friendly and clearly safe for a toddler audience.
